aboutH2: Psychedelic-assisted therapy in Sault Ste. Marie
intro: Field Trip Health Sault Ste. Marie is a small outpatient clinic on the third floor of the Elgin Tower at 390 Bay Street, downtown. For people in Algoma who want ketamine-assisted psychotherapy, it is the only Field Trip clinic within several hours' drive; the nearest others are in Thunder Bay and southern Ontario.

The clinic treats adults with depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, chronic pain and substance use problems, usually after other treatment has fallen short. Everything happens in daytime appointments from Monday to Friday, and you go home the same day. Its therapists are mainly registered social workers, and it lists clients coming from Bruce Mines, Thessalon, Blind River, Elliot Lake and across the river in Michigan.

pillars.title: What a dosing day looks like
pillars.body: Plan for about two and a half hours at the clinic. A nurse gives the medicine, most often as an injection into the arm muscle, while you rest in a zero-gravity chair with a weighted blanket and headphones playing a chosen playlist. Your therapist stays in the room the whole time, and before you go you talk through what came up. Someone else has to drive you home afterwards.

pillars.title: A quiet suite above Bay Street
pillars.body: The clinic is in Suite 303 of the Elgin Tower. Go in through the double glass doors, follow the hallway to the elevators and ride up to the third floor; the suite is at the end of the hall. Free parking is set aside in the centre two rows of the Elgin Tower lot, and the clinic is on local transit routes. The space is wheelchair accessible, and service animals are welcome.

pillars.title: A small, experienced local team
pillars.body: Therapy in Sault Ste. Marie is provided mainly by registered social workers. The team page names Ashley Irwin, RSW, MA, and Deborah Irwin, a registered psychotherapist with more than 40 years of work with children, youth, adults and families. Registered nurse Chantale Vallieres works with Nick Campbell on the medical side, and nurse practitioners across the Field Trip network run the screening consults.

overviewH2: How the Sault Ste. Marie program works
overview: The first contact is a free 15-minute discovery call. If it sounds like a fit, you fill in a questionnaire and book a 50-minute consultation with a nurse practitioner, which OHIP does not cover. That appointment is where safety is checked. The clinic says the treatment may not suit people who are pregnant, have had psychosis or schizophrenia, have uncontrolled high blood pressure or a recent severe head injury.

Once approved, most people work through 6 or 9 dosing sessions of roughly two and a half hours each. The medicine is usually an intramuscular injection, and a therapist is with you for the whole session. Some of the nurse practitioners are based in other Field Trip clinics, so ask on your discovery call whether the consult happens in person or online.

faqIntro: Answers are drawn from the Sault Ste. Marie clinic's page on fieldtriphealth.ca. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Field Trip Health Sault Ste. Marie a rehab centre where I stay overnight?
faqs.a: No. It is an outpatient clinic with weekday appointments, and you go home after each one. There are no beds, meals or detox services. If you need residential addiction treatment or withdrawal support, raise it on the discovery call or compare live-in programs elsewhere in Ontario.

faqs.q: What is psychedelic-assisted therapy used for in Sault Ste. Marie?
faqs.a: The clinic offers ketamine-assisted psychotherapy mainly for depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, addiction and chronic pain, usually for people who have already tried medication or counselling. Its therapists also see clients for grief, ADHD, eating disorders, bipolar disorder, complex PTSD and relationship difficulties. Outcomes vary, and the clinic does not promise results.

faqs.q: How much does treatment cost in Sault Ste. Marie?
faqs.a: The clinic does not post prices online; the cost depends on how many sessions you need and how the medicine is given, and the team explains it on a free discovery call. The nurse practitioner consultation is a paid appointment that OHIP does not cover. Extended health benefits for psychotherapy or nursing often cover part of the cost, and third-party financing is available.

faqs.q: How long does each session take?
faqs.a: About 2.5 hours, according to the clinic, including preparation, the medicine and integration support. A standard plan has 6 or 9 dosing sessions, and afterwards the team helps you decide what ongoing care, if any, you need.

Adults who pass a medical consultation with a nurse practitioner. The clinic says it may not be suitable if you are pregnant, are allergic to the medicine, have a personal history of schizophrenia or psychosis, uncontrolled hypertension or a severe recent head injury. You can book the first call yourself, or your doctor can refer you.

faqs.q: Where is the clinic and how do I find it?
faqs.a: It is at 390 Bay Street, Suite 303, in the Elgin Tower in downtown Sault Ste. Marie. Enter through the double glass doors, take the elevators to the third floor and go to the end of the hall. Free parking is in the centre two rows of the Elgin Tower lot, and the building is reachable by city transit.

faqs.q: I live outside the city. Is this clinic my closest option?
faqs.a: For much of Algoma, yes. Field Trip Health lists Sault Ste. Marie as the nearest clinic for places such as Goulais River, Searchmont, Bruce Mines, Thessalon, Blind River, Elliot Lake and Spanish, as well as Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan. Remember you will need a driver after each dosing session, which matters if you live an hour or more away.
Yes. The Sault Ste. Marie clinic is wheelchair accessible, with elevator access to the third floor, and it welcomes service animals.

faqs.q: What should I do before a session?
faqs.a: Skip alcohol and recreational drugs, avoid a heavy meal, and arrange a ride home because you may feel drowsy afterwards. Bring up any medications you take during your consultation so the nurse practitioner can review them.

faqs.q: Is this the same company as Field Trip Health in the US?
faqs.a: Not any more. Field Trip Health's Canadian clinics, including Sault Ste. Marie, have run as Field Trip Health Canada since the 2023 restructuring, when they were taken over by the Canadian Centre for Psychedelic Healing. The US clinics belong to a different company, so book through fieldtriphealth.ca.
